analysis:
All changes in this batch are test-only Swift files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests: ModelAutopilotTests.swift (new tests at head lines 122-166), TransitionWatchdogTests.swift (new, 207 lines) and AutopilotTinyModelTests.swift (new, 243 lines, with only the patch excerpt visible and no head text). No production source is modified in this batch, so no trust-boundary, key-custody, attestation, encryption or authorization control is weakened here.

Behavior the tests describe, which the integration pass should check against production code that is not in this batch:
- The coordinator-controlled `hold_seconds` field in the model_autopilot command is bounded to 0...86400 and rejected when there is no load target. The coordinator is trusted, but the provider still validates it as defence in depth. Production enforcement is in ModelAutopilotPolicy, which is not supplied.
- Status `detail` is optional on the wire, and `startup_preload` is reported as a busy reason. This is a non-sensitive enumerated string.
- The transition watchdog is consent-gated (`withoutConsentTheWatchdogNeitherActsNorReports`), reports stalls, and never interrupts in-flight loads. A stalled startup preload only stops before its next model. This is an availability-oriented control (T-010/T-029 area). Whether production consent gating matches this test needs a look at the non-test source.
- The adopted-inventory test claims a model stays advertised and served after the autopilot lease ends until an admin unload. If production keeps serving after the lease ends, check that this does not bypass the consent or selection checks (A-016/TB-011 boundary). That is unverifiable from the supplied excerpt, so I record it as a question rather than a finding.

No secrets, new network surface or plaintext exposure appear in the tests. The AutopilotTinyModelTests.swift patch is truncated, so it was only partially examined.
